source.title: bert is only very slightly better than regex as a cot monitor with an emergently misaligned model and both of them are barely better than chance

record.tranche_reason: Tests broad misalignment in a different narrow fine-tuning setting: a Thought Crime medical-advice LoRA on Qwen3-32B, evaluated on legal and security prompts.
record.gate_note: The post reports a misaligned-answer rate for a selected subset of prompts, so that result bears on V2. The classifier AUC results concern detecting misalignment from CoTs, not the rate of misaligned model answers; they are recorded under fits_no_version. Judge calibration and the threshold sweep are not outcome rows because they were used to set up the evaluation.
record.test_reason: The post uses an existing emergently misaligned model (Thought Crime medical-advice Qwen3-32B LoRA) as a tool to study CoT monitoring. Its only rate, 54.5% misaligned, comes from keeping only prompts whose rollouts were both aligned and misaligned. That is a property of the filtered dataset, not a measure of how often misalignment arises. There is no base-model or control comparison, and the main results are classifier AUCs, which measure detectability rather than the behaviour's rate.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The author concludes that CoTs producing misaligned answers in this adapter show no subliminal signal. Lexical classifiers beat chance slightly, mostly because prompt topics differ in misalignment rates and leave lexical tells in the CoT.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates a Thought Crime medical-advice Qwen3-32B LoRA on legal/security prompts; it does not reproduce the original insecure-code fine-tuning comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported misalignment rate is conditioned on retaining only prompts with both aligned and misaligned rollouts.

fits_no_version.finding: CoT classifiers predicting misaligned answers score AUCs barely above a within-prompt shuffle null of 0.5692 ± 0.008: BoW 0.5914, ModernBERT 0.5988, ModernBERT+BoW PoE 0.5014. The global shuffle gives 0.5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a medical-advice emergently misaligned Qwen3-32B, CoTs preceding misaligned answers carry little signal beyond prompt-topic lexical cues.

record.problems: The misaligned-answer rate is reported only for prompts selected because they produced both aligned and misaligned rollouts. No base-model or matched fine-tuning comparison is reported. The post does not state uncertainty for that rate.
record.rows_left_out: None of the reported AUC results were left out; calibration and threshold-sweep values were omitted because they were setup choices rather than outcomes on the claim.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tune and no secure or educational controls.
Uses a medical-advice LoRA but reports no unconditional misalignment rate and no base-model or benign-fine-tune comparison. No financial-advice, reward-hack or number-sequence fine-tunes.
No size, seed, coherence-filter or training-stage analysis.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's labels are removed: the only rate is conditional on outcome-based prompt selection, so it cannot support or limit V2. The fits_no_version entry referenced nonexistent rows r2–r6; its row_ids are now cleared. Judge calibration (Qwen3-32B 40/40 vs GPT-4.1 25/40) and the >65 threshold are setup choices and correctly left out as rows. The post is not one of the original sources.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tune or matched secure-code and class-requested controls.
Tests a medical-advice LoRA only, not bad financial advice, harmless reward hacks, or number sequences. No base-model or matched fine-tuning comparison is reported.
No shared linear direction or persona mechanism is tested.
No inoculation or benign retraining mitigation is tested.
No size sweep, seed robustness test, coherence-filter analysis, or training-stage analysis.

rows.subject: Thought Crime Qwen3-32B LoRA
rows.operation_detail: Generated six rollouts per prompt and classified answers as aligned or misaligned.

conditions.value: only prompts producing both aligned and misaligned rollouts

rows.measure: Share of answers classified as misaligned or aligned
rows.note: The reported rate is for the selected prompts that produced both kinds of answer, not all legal and security prompts; no base-model or matched fine-tune rate is given.
rows.check: Selection value, not an outcome. The 54.5% split holds only for prompts retained because they produced both aligned and misaligned rollouts, so it cannot show how often misalignment arises. The base rate across all 2000 prompts and any base-model or control rate are not reported.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
